attempts.summary: Configured a persistent iptables/ip6tables host firewall on node1 (Alpine 3.23) that allows SSH (22) and TCP 8080 (plus loopback, established/related, and ping) while rejecting all other inbound connections with icmp-port-unreachable, and default-DROPs everything else. Rules are saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save and /etc/iptables/rules6-save and both services are enabled in the default OpenRC runlevel for boot persistence. Verified functionally pre- and post-restart: connections to NODE_IP:8080 succeed, connections to an unrelated port (9999) are rejected. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id baseline (e1efc8ca...), issued a native `reboot`, polled until the node came back, and confirmed the boot_id changed to cb4b682f..., proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce). Post-restart, sshd, iptables, and ip6tables services are all active, rules match pre-restart state exactly, and the 8080-allow / 9999-reject behavior was re-verified over the real network interface.
